title: The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data
main_claim: Take uniform odd integer heights on triangular-lattice approximations of a smooth simply connected domain, with neighbouring differences 0 or 2 and boundary values +1 and -1 on two arcs. As the mesh goes to zero they converge in distributions to the harmonic extension of the boundary data plus sigma times the Dirichlet GFF, with joint moment convergence. Here sigma = 4*pi*sqrt(c_*) > 0, and c_* is given by an absolutely convergent series of finite-volume counts.
coverage:
I read all ten sections of build/sections/*.tex. These parts were checked line by line, with the computations verified:
(a) Section 2: the Gray-code increment dH=(W_xB_y-B_xW_y)/2 and the residue table; the two-spin FKG proof via supermodular F2 nullity (the triangle split between ++ and -- edges); the exact cut law.
(b) Section 3: local and buffer circuit gluing; the loop estimates; the rare-pin sandwich c_1 q <= lambda(A) <= q, including the FKG step that justifies the lower bound; the pin-product argument.
(c) Section 4: the dyadic midpoint tail recursion (interval arithmetic and the doubly exponential iteration); the component-switch identity d(H+BW/2)=W dB giving shifts of +-4; the parity-class transitivity for obstacle moments; the equal-offset corollary.
(d) Section 5: the anchored-phase reflection positivity factorisation; the log-convexity contraction; the exclusion of the tilt term; the Cauchy-mixture identification, where the Fourier coefficients of Q_s are e^{-sqrt3 s|j|}. The angular Poisson identity checks: Poisson extension of ((a+iz)/(a-iz))^2 gives ((a-s)/(a+s))^2. The zero sixfold average of cos 4theta checks, as does the negativity region |l/k| < 1+sqrt2. Frullani gives log|cos u|, and int cos4u log|cos u| = -pi/2 from the Fourier coefficient -1/2. The constant v=(2pi)^2 c_* follows from Plancherel and the log-kernel convention.
(e) Section 6: b_j=-2I_j, hence c_*=(1/pi)sum b_j; the finite-volume error bounds; sigma=2sqrt(v)=4pi sqrt(c_*).
(f) Section 7: the bracket interval table; the normalized reflection bound; the analytic-translation (normal families) argument. I checked the three-direction move sequence using u.e=1/2 and u.u'=-1/2, the Fourier projection onto equal offsets, the gap-filling coupling and the 2eps/c conditioning bound, and the bracket identity truncation.
(g) Section 8: the synthetic anchored comparison and its domination; the label-flip symmetry giving mean k-1/2; the cell-mean inequality giving P(U) >= 1/2 - o(1); the bulk loop-sign circuit; exponential amplification.
(h) Section 9: tightness; bracket squeeze to H^-=H=H^+; boundary traces; the reference averages; the transport identity and the separation geometry; the no-diagonal lemma.
(i) Section 10: the log-singularity lemma; the stopped plane coupling; the collision coefficient v/(2pi)T_{j-2}, consistent with vG_D; the Gaussian recursion and moment determinacy.
I also checked that the companion annulus theorem (weighted paper Thm 2.3/thm:circuit-input, at x=1 and a=2, with B=- on the boundary layer and W free) matches how it is used in Lemma 3.2. Read only at proof-structure level: the planar-topology details of the arch/attachment constructions (U cap L subset A) and the distributional step in Lemma 5.8 (rotation and translation invariance implying a constant density).
